### Day 269: Acts 19:21–31
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-269-acts-19-2131.html
Passage: Acts 19:21-31
Points:
- Financial loss motivated Demetrius and the craftsmen to stir up a riot against Paul.
- Paul demonstrated immense courage by desiring to face the hostile crowd directly in the theater.
- Wise Christian leaders are not dictators; Paul listened and yielded to the judgment of his companions.
- Believers should employ God-given good sense rather than recklessly stepping into danger without divine direction.
- Paul developed genuine friendships across diverse backgrounds, including local officials who intervened to protect him.

### Peace Amidst Unpleasant Circumstances
Author: Pastor Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/peace-amidst-unpleasant-circumstances?ga=testimonial-resources
Passage: Acts 19:23-31
Points:
- Serious disturbances often arise right after believers surrender their lives and plans to God.
- Demetrius made Paul a scapegoat because genuine faith was destroying the trade in silver idols.
- Clinging to Christ frees people from needing artificial religious symbols and trinkets.
- Surrendered believers experience God's supernatural peace rather than giving in to mob-driven panic.
- God calls His followers to stay calm and honor Him through confusing and hostile trials.
